text:
Tom: quick question — Acme POC wants an on-prem evaluation in their data center. they asked if we can waive the one-time platform fee for the POC and only charge support.

Olivia: how long is the POC and expected infra footprint? that usually affects our stance on waiving fees.

Tom: 6 weeks, single rack GPU, small persistent KV cache, only ~200k tokens/day expected. goal is integration + latency verification.

Kai: tech note: they need KMS/HSM integration for keys and want us to run the control plane in their VPC. doable in Private tier but adds ops lift. also will need a short SLA for POC (business hours on-call).

Maria: commercial ask — they want Platform Fee waived for POC. instead propose we apply a refundable trial deposit of $15k that becomes credit if they convert within 90 days. keeps skin in the game. thoughts? :thinking_face:

Raj: can we give a support-tier discount instead? e.g., waive platform fee + charge Standard support at 10% of list for POC length. then if they commit to Dedicated/Private, we roll that into the first invoice.

Olivia: Acme is enterprise — they'd likely sign for Dedicated if latency checks out. I prefer refundable deposit or a small discounted platform fee, not full waiver, to avoid precedent.

FinanceBot: FYI — platform fee typically $40k one-time for Private, Standard support 12% MRC, Enterprise support 20% MRC. refundable deposit reduces ARR recognition until conversion.

Tom: Legal asked about special terms: they want a 30-day indemnity clause and to remove export controls paragraph for POC infra. LegalBot, any red flags?

LegalBot: removing export controls is a no. we can offer a limited indemnity for the POC scope only. any changes to standard T&Cs require legal review — will take ~3 business days.

Raj: deal desk decision request: recommend refundable deposit $15k + Standard support at 10% for 6 weeks, waiving the platform fee for the POC only. If conversion within 60 days, deposit credits first month. If no conversion, deposit refunded less admin fee $1k.

Maria: alternatively propose 50% platform fee ($20k) paid upfront, refundable upon conversion. which is cleaner for accounting?

FinanceBot: accounting prefers refundable deposit as liability — cleaner than recognizing half-platform fee then refund. deposit avoids revenue deferral complexity.

Olivia: we also need to confirm SLA: for POC we can offer Business Hours support (8x5) with 4hr response, and a named SE for on-site coordination if needed (time-and-expense). Enterprise on-call requires Enterprise support tier.

Kai: technical checklist for POC (to add to SOW): KMS endpoints, VPC peering, instance SKU list, baseline perf tests, canary rollout policy. add KV prefix caching limits. I'll draft.

Tom: can deal desk approve refundable deposit + 10% support discount for POC and sign-off for limited legal POC indemnity? this is blocking the sales cycle this week.

Raj: +1 from me, will escalate to Deal Desk. tagging @deal-desk for approval.

FinanceBot: tagging pricing team for one-off: pricing@redwood — reference deal: ACME-POC-031.

Olivia: thanks — I'll send the SOW draft with deposit terms and POC SLA once Kai shares checklist.

Tom: perfect. ping me if you need numbers to justify discount to the AE. :thumbsup:

Kai: draft checklist uploaded to the Google drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example (will replace with real link in SOW).

LegalBot: I'll start the limited-terms addendum and aim to have a redline within 48 hours.

Deal-desk: any blocking questions before I propose this structure to Acme?

Maria: just confirm refundable deposit amount and the admin fee on refund. otherwise i'm good.

FinanceBot: admin fee $1k ok from finance for processing refunds.

Tom: thanks all — will prep customer-facing proposal now and loop back when deal-desk confirms. :rocket:
